payload.task_text:
I am an assessment coordinator and I need help analyzing the quality of quiz questions across our Fall 2014 semester courses. There is a PDF file in the workspace called Assessment_Standards.pdf that describes how to compute item difficulty indices and quality ratings for quizzes, please refer to it for the methodology.

Pull all quiz and question data from the learning management system for the Fall 2014 courses (course codes ending in 2014J). For each quiz, compute the average score from submission data, then calculate the difficulty index as average score divided by 100 since scores are on a percentage scale. Classify each quiz's difficulty as Easy (above 0.7), Optimal (0.3 to 0.7), or Hard (below 0.3). Also compute the completion rate as the number of submissions divided by enrolled students for each course. A quiz's quality rating depends on what percentage of its questions fall in the optimal difficulty range. Since we are using quiz-level difficulty as a proxy for all questions in that quiz, each quiz either has 100% optimal questions or 0%. Rate quizzes as Excellent if more than 70% of questions are optimal, Good if 50-70%, and Needs Review if below 50%.

Note that some Fall 2014 courses may not have any quizzes at all. Only include courses that actually have quiz data in the quiz-level sheets, but include all 7 Fall 2014 courses in the course summary, showing zero quizzes and questions for those without quiz data.

Create an Excel file called Quiz_Item_Analysis.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet called Quiz Overview should have columns Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Points_Possible, Submission_Count, Avg_Score rounded to 1 decimal, Completion_Rate_Pct rounded to 1 decimal, and Quality_Rating. Sort rows by course name then quiz title. The second sheet called Question Analysis should have columns Course_Name, Quiz_Title, Question_Position, Question_Type, Points_Possible, and Difficulty_Category showing Easy, Optimal, or Hard for each question. One row per question, using the quiz-level difficulty as the proxy for all questions in that quiz. The third sheet called Course Summary should have columns Course_Name sorted alphabetically, Total_Quizzes, Total_Questions, Excellent_Quizzes, Good_Quizzes, Review_Quizzes, and Avg_Completion_Rate rounded to 1 decimal. Include all 7 Fall 2014 courses even if they have no quizzes. All numeric cells (submission counts, averages, completion rates) must be written as literal numbers, not Excel formulas. Avg_Completion_Rate for a course is the average of that course's per-quiz completion rates (sum of the quiz completion rates divided by the number of quizzes), rounded to 1 decimal. For a course with no quizzes, Avg_Completion_Rate is undefined: write 0 (or leave the cell blank / 'N/A'); do not invent a percentage.

Write a Word document called Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx with sections for Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Findings covering each Fall 2014 course that has quizzes, Question Type Analysis breaking down performance by question type, Recommendations for improving quiz quality, and an Appendix.

Schedule 7 quiz review sessions on the calendar, one for each Fall 2014 course. Each session should be 45 minutes long, scheduled on weekdays during the week of March 16-20, 2026 (Monday through Friday). Title each event Quiz Review - followed by the course name. Spread them across the week so that no two sessions overlap: for example, at most two review sessions per weekday and ensure each session starts and ends within business hours (09:00-17:00). Use UTC as the timezone for all events: pass event start/end times as ISO timestamps with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. ending in 'Z' or '+00:00'), and set each event's timezone field to UTC. Business hours (09:00-17:00) refer to UTC.

Finally send an email to assessment_office@university.edu with a subject line about quiz item analysis findings and a body summarizing the overall results including how many courses had quizzes, the difficulty distribution, and quality ratings.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep all quiz-submission and question reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave of three course-sharded collectors, freeze the gathered statistics into one merged JSON handoff file, and let the main agent itself build every deliverable — no planning sub-agent, no second wave.

The main agent first reads Assessment_Standards.pdf in the runtime workspace for the literal difficulty/quality methodology, resolves the workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the seven Fall 2014 courses (codes ending 2014J). It captures each course's enrollment denominator, then natively in parallel calls the quiz listing once per course and freezes the quiz-bearing manifest with literal IDs — expected: course_id 7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" quizzes [20,21,22,23]; course_id 17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" quizzes [52,53,54,55,56,57,58]; course_id 21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" quizzes [71,72,73,74,75,76]. Courses without quizzes stay in the course summary with zeros.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per quiz-bearing course below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=7 "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" quizzes [20,21,22,23]. For each of its quizzes call canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id, quiz_id) following pagination, always reading the FULL JSON from the output_path file when the chat preview is truncated; each submission carries a string score on a 0-100 percentage scale. Fetch the quiz's question data (question positions, types, points possible) through the quiz-question listing. Compute per quiz: Submission_Count, Avg_Score (mean of scores, keep unrounded internally), difficulty index = avg/100 with categories Easy (>0.7) / Optimal (0.3-0.7) / Hard (<0.3), and the quiz-level quality rating via the quiz-difficulty proxy (Excellent / Good / Needs Review thresholds per the standards document). Return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id, course_name, enrolled_students, quizzes: [{quiz_id, quiz_title, points_possible, submission_count, avg_score, difficulty_index, difficulty_category, quality_rating, questions: [{position, type, points_possible}]}]}. Strictly read-only with respect to Canvas; do not write workspace files, do not return the raw row set.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=17 "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" quizzes [52,53,54,55,56,57,58] — same literal recipe, only the course and quiz list substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=21 "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" quizzes [71,72,73,74,75,76] — same literal recipe, only the course and quiz list substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent verifies the three handoffs in one single pass, merges everything into workspace/merged_quiz_data.json — the single handoff for the outputs — and computes completion rates (submissions divided by the course's enrolled students) and per-course aggregates (Avg_Completion_Rate = mean of per-quiz completion rates; zero/blank for quiz-less courses). It then directly, with no further delegation: (a) creates Quiz_Item_Analysis.xlsx with exactly three sheets per the task contract — Quiz Overview (only courses with quizzes, sorted Course_Name then Quiz_Title), Question Analysis (one row per question, quiz-level Difficulty_Category as proxy), Course Summary (all 7 Fall 2014 courses, zeroed for quiz-less courses) — all numerics literal (no formulas), Avg_Score and completion percentages rounded to 1 decimal, and reads the populated ranges back; (b) writes Quiz_Analysis_Report.docx with the sections Executive Summary, Methodology, Course-by-Course Findings (each course with quizzes), Question Type Analysis, Recommendations, Appendix, using only metrics present in the merged JSON; (c) schedules 7 quiz review sessions of 45 minutes on Google Calendar for the week 2026-03-16..2026-03-20, titled "Quiz Review - {Course_Name}", alphabetically assigned to fixed UTC slots (09:00-09:45 UTC each of the five weekdays, plus 11:00-11:45 UTC on 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-20), all timestamps explicit ISO 8601 UTC, skipping any event that already exists; (d) sends the summary email to assessment_office@university.edu exactly once and reads it back. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back, the document, the seven calendar events and the sent message, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

You are gathering READ-ONLY data from Canvas (via the canvas MCP tools) for a quiz item analysis. Do not create, update, or delete anything.

CONTEXT: I am analyzing all Fall 2014 courses (course codes ending in 2014J) in Canvas. Three of them have quizzes:
- Course 7 = "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)": quizzes 20 (CMA 24295), 21 (CMA 24296), 22 (CMA 24297), 23 (CMA 24298)
- Course 17 = "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)": quizzes 52 (CMA 34904), 53 (CMA 34905), 54 (CMA 34906), 55 (CMA 34907), 56 (CMA 34908), 57 (CMA 34910), 58 (CMA 34909)
- Course 21 = "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)": quizzes 71 (CMA 37438), 72 (CMA 37439), 73 (CMA 37440), 74 (CMA 37441), 75 (CMA 37442), 76 (CMA 37443)

TASK A — Quiz submission dumps (16 calls, skip quiz 20 which is already dumped):
For each (course_id, quiz_id) pair below, call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions(course_id, quiz_id):
(7,21), (7,22), (7,23), (17,52), (17,53), (17,54), (17,55), (17,56), (17,57), (17,58), (21,71), (21,72), (21,73), (21,74), (21,75), (21,76)
These responses are large and automatically dumped to text files under /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace/.tool_results/ with names like mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions-call_<callid>-<uuid>.txt. Record the EXACT output file path reported for each quiz_id (the tool result includes an "output_path" field when the output is dumped). If any response is NOT dumped (shown inline instead), note "inline" for that quiz_id along with its submission count and average score if easily computable.

TASK B — Question metadata (17 calls):
For each of the 17 quizzes above PLUS quiz (7,20), call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_questions(course_id, quiz_id). For EVERY question returned, extract only: quiz_id, position, question_type, points_possible.

DELIVERABLE — your final message must contain exactly two sections:
1. "SUBMISSION DUMPS:" — one line per quiz_id: "<quiz_id> -> <exact file path or 'inline'>" (17 lines total, including quiz 20 marked as already-dumped with its file path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-quiz-item-analysis-word-gcal-email/workspace/.tool_results/mcp__canvas__canvas_list_quiz_submissions-call_d335b9cde79c4c56a598ae14-1a26d078-8388-40d0-8723-679cd3fdddc9.txt if that file exists).
2. "QUESTIONS CSV:" — a CSV block with header "quiz_id,position,question_type,points_possible" followed by one row per question for all 17 quizzes (expected total rows ≈ 345). Sort rows by quiz_id then position. Do not truncate — include every question.

QUALITY CHECK: expected question counts per quiz: 20:27, 21:17, 22:20, 23:29, 52:26, 53:29, 54:22, 55:24, 56:10, 57:12, 58:12, 71:21, 72:23, 73:25, 74:22, 75:10, 76:16. If any actual count differs from expected, flag it explicitly in a third section "DISCREPANCIES:". If a question list is empty, flag it too.

Do not read the large submission dump files (they are too big); just record their paths.
Pull Canvas quiz questions data
